steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Composition in photography is about what you INCLUDE and EXCLUDE from the frame — every element should have a purpose. | Key Fact: The rule of thirds places subjects at intersection points for dynamic balance; centre placement creates formality or stillness. | Key Fact: Leading lines guide the viewer's eye through the image — roads, fences, rivers, shadows all work as leading lines. | Key Fact: Viewpoint changes meaning: low angle = power; high angle = vulnerability; eye level = neutrality; dutch angle = tension.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring composition and framing. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with composition and framing. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed you | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with composition and framing. Which approaches were most successful and why?
